about.heroCopy: Black diamonds are not born of typical earth-bound pressures. These enigmatic polycrystalline structures carry the weight of celestial origins, offering a depth that absorbs light and redefines the meaning of brilliance.
narrativeBody: Every stone in our catalog is meticulously sourced from deep metamorphic cratons, ensuring that the void within each gem is as pure as it is profound.
We do not chase brilliance. We preserve gravity. BlackDiamond exists to bring the most serious black diamonds in the world to the collectors who understand what they represent.
Each acquisition is supported by gemological documentation, provenance records, and a curatorial point of view built on fifteen years of fieldwork.
about.manifesto: Light passes through most things. Black diamonds consume it. In a world that celebrates sparkle, we celebrate weight — the irreducible presence of matter that has survived billions of years to exist in your hand.

education.title: The alchemy of darkness
education.intro: Black diamonds are geological anomalies: opaque, polycrystalline diamonds shaped by extreme pressure, time, and mystery.
originBody: Unlike traditional diamonds that crystallize deep within the mantle, the origin story of black diamonds remains debated.
Their porous structure and unusual signatures have inspired both terrestrial and cosmic theories.

properties.title: Indomitable toughness
properties.body: A polycrystalline structure makes many black diamonds exceptionally resistant to cleavage.

properties.title: The porous void
properties.body: Internal porosity gives black diamonds a distinct density and surface character.

properties.title: Total opacity
properties.body: Graphite and mineral inclusions create the deep black visual signature.

education.originQuote: Black diamonds are the only diamonds found on Earth that are never associated with Kimberlite pipes — the volcanic highways that bring mantle diamonds to the surface.
education.originEvidenceBody: Infrared spectroscopy reveals that black diamonds contain trace elements of polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons — building blocks of stars.
education.rarityCardBody: Black diamonds are found exclusively in the Central African Republic and Brazil, never in the same mining sites as common diamonds.
education.rawBody: In natural form, black diamonds can resemble charcoal: irregular, rugged, and marked by intense formation history.
education.cutBody: When polished, a black diamond reveals a metallic, sub-adamantine luster unlike transparent gemstones.
education.caratBody: Black diamonds command attention not through sparkle, but through weight and silhouette.

regions.name: Brazil — Carbonado Capital
regions.body: The carbonado of Brazil represents the largest known source of natural black diamonds. Found in alluvial deposits far from any kimberlite pipe, these stones are characterized by a denser polycrystalline matrix and higher graphite inclusion density, producing a deep, light-consuming black.

regions.name: Central African Republic
regions.body: CAR stones exhibit more surface porosity and a distinctive matte-to-metallic luster range. Their alluvial distribution pattern aligns closely with the extraterrestrial impact theory, lending them a provenance narrative unlike any other gemstone on Earth.

education.gradingIntro: Unlike colorless diamonds graded on the 4Cs, black diamonds are evaluated through a distinct framework built around opacity, structure, and surface character.

gradingCriteria.title: Surface Luster
gradingCriteria.body: Ranges from matte to sub-adamantine to metallic. Metallic luster is the rarest and commands the highest premium in collector markets.

gradingCriteria.title: Inclusion Density
gradingCriteria.body: The distribution of graphite and hematite inclusions determines the uniformity of black color. Even, dense distribution is preferred over patchy or transparent zones.

gradingCriteria.title: Structural Integrity
gradingCriteria.body: Unlike single-crystal diamonds, black diamonds are assessed for polycrystalline cohesion — the absence of separating grain boundaries visible under magnification.

gradingCriteria.title: Surface Character
gradingCriteria.body: The visibility of porous microstructure is documented. High-grade stones show minimal surface pitting under 10× magnification and maximum facet reflectivity.

education.cuttingIntro: Cutting a black diamond is categorically more complex than cutting a colorless stone. The polycrystalline structure requires a completely different methodology.

cuttingSteps.title: Structural Mapping
cuttingSteps.body: Before any saw touches the stone, gemologists map polycrystalline grain boundaries using polarized light. Cutting across a grain line risks fracture propagation through the entire stone.

cuttingSteps.title: Laser Shaping
cuttingSteps.body: Initial shaping uses a laser rather than a mechanical saw. The precision reduces thermal stress and the fracture risk common in polycrystalline material.

cuttingSteps.title: Facet Planning
cuttingSteps.body: Unlike transparent stones, black diamonds are faceted to maximize silhouette and surface luster — not light return. Every geometric decision is purely aesthetic and architectural.

cuttingSteps.title: Metallic Polishing
cuttingSteps.body: A specialized iron scaife charged with diamond powder polishes each facet to a metallic finish. The process takes 3–4× longer than polishing a colorless diamond of equivalent size.
